sections.h2: How do I contact the Granville County Register of Deeds in Oxford?
sections.html:
Go to the courthouse at 101 Main Street, Oxford, NC 27565, or call 919-693-6314. The mailing address is P.O. Box 427, Oxford, NC 27565.

The county's online ordering page gives office hours as Monday through Friday, 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM, and says a request sent after 4 PM waits until the next business day. For a sale, phone first and ask what the staff will need for your type of instrument, since they may not draft or repair documents.

The register of deeds is a countywide elected position, and G.S. 161-1 sets the term at two years.

sections.h2: Which documents does the Oxford office file?
sections.html:
Real estate records are the core of its work: deeds, deeds of trust, cancellations, plats, assumed names, powers of attorney and similar instruments. The county says each is recorded, indexed and scanned, and that deed records stretch back to 1746.

  • Land records: deeds, deeds of trust, plats and cancellations.
  • Personal records: births, deaths, marriages and marriage licenses.
  • Other filings: military discharges and notary commissions, plus the oath for Granville County notaries.

Staff run a recording counter, not a legal clinic. The office tells filers that state law bars it from practicing law, so it will not supply legal forms, coach you through filling one in, or say what a recorded document means legally. A North Carolina attorney can answer those questions.

sections.h2: What does Granville charge for vital records ordered online?
sections.html:
A certified birth, marriage or death certificate is $10.00 each, and an uncertified copy is $1.00, with a non-refundable $4 service and card fee on every online order. Records on the system begin in 1913.

Online vital record prices on the Granville County Register of Deeds ordering page (https://granvillecounty.org/731/Online-Ordering-Vital-Records)

A copy of a valid photo ID is required with every request. Anyone newly married should wait 10 days after the ceremony before ordering a certified marriage copy. Death certificates may also be picked up by a funeral director who shows license proof.

sections.h2: What does it cost to put a deed on the Granville County record?
sections.html:
Two charges apply: the statewide recording fee and the transfer excise tax. The fee schedule comes from G.S. 161-10 and does not vary by county.

  • A general instrument is $26.00 up to 15 pages, then $4.00 for each added page.
  • A deed of trust or mortgage is $64.00 up to 35 pages, then $4.00 per page after that.
  • Cancellations and satisfactions of deeds of trust are free to record.

The seller pays the excise tax of $1.00 per $500 of value, with any fraction of $500 counting as a full unit. G.S. 105-228.30 requires it before the clerk records the deed. Half the tax remains with the county, and the rest goes to the state each month. For land spread over two or more counties, the county holding the greater value collects. The statute figures the tax off the consideration, so the number stated on the deed should match the contract.

sections.h2: Why should a Granville County deed be recorded promptly?
sections.html:
Registration is what makes a land instrument effective against third parties. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance, option, lease longer than three years or right of first refusal does not bind lien creditors or later buyers until it is registered in the county where the land is.

Priority goes to whoever registers first, by time. If you sell on a contract for deed, Chapter 47H adds that the seller must record the contract, or a Memorandum of a Contract for Deed, within five business days. The buyer under such a contract may cancel until midnight on the third business day after signing or delivery, and a forfeiture requires a written notice with a cure date at least 30 days out.

sections.h2: Is there protection against property fraud in Granville County?
sections.html:
Yes. The register of deeds' office provides a free alert tool, PropertyCheck, through its software vendor. Owners can ask for an email or text whenever a document is recorded that matches a name, a street address or a parcel number.

  • Register on the vendor's website.
  • Create alerts for each version of your name and for your spouse.
  • Add the property address and parcel number.

The county describes the scheme it guards against: a forger moves title into another name and records the paperwork while the real owner stays unaware. An alert does not block a filing. It gives you the chance to call 919-693-6314 and consult a lawyer fast.

sections.h2: What goes to the Register of Deeds, and what goes to the clerk of court?
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Register of Deeds. Probate matters go to the clerk of superior court. If an owner died, a small estate affidavit under G.S. 28A-25-1 is filed with the clerk in the county where the decedent lived, and the statute lists a description of each tract of real property the decedent owned.

The personal property ceiling for that route is $20,000 after liens, or up to $30,000 for a sole-heir surviving spouse after any spousal allowance, and 30 days must pass after death before filing. A bigger estate needs a different procedure from the clerk, which this page does not cover. Once the right to sell is established, the deed that results is still recorded at the Oxford courthouse counter.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about the Granville County housing stock?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counts 25,685 housing units for 2025 and 22,474 households for 2020 to 2024, with 2.52 people in a typical household.

  • Veterans living in the county: 3,363.
  • Building permits in 2025: 257.
  • Share of residents in the same home a year earlier: 90.4%.
  • Monthly owner cost with a mortgage, middle figure: $1,546.
  • Poverty rate: 13.5%.

These county medians frame the market, but recording fees and excise tax follow state law and are not affected by them.

faqs.q: What is the fee for a general deed in Granville County?
faqs.a: $26.00 for up to 15 pages, then $4.00 for every added page, under G.S. 161-10. The seller also owes the excise tax of $1.00 per $500 of value.
Monday through Friday, 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM per the county's online ordering page. The phone number is 919-693-6314.

faqs.q: Will the Register of Deeds draft my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office is a recording office, and North Carolina law keeps its staff from practicing law, so it cannot supply forms or advise on legal effect. Hire an attorney for drafting.

faqs.q: Do I pay to file a deed of trust cancellation?
faqs.a: No. G.S. 161-10 lists no fee for recording a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust or mortgage.

faqs.q: How old are the deed records here?
faqs.a: The county page says deeds are available back to 1746, while vital records ordered online start in 1913.
